title: panel-telemetry-experiments-lab-log-2027-02-11
content:
Context:
Quick lab log from the Tuesday slot where the panel & analytics subteam paired on a set of telemetry experiments intended to reduce noisy rollouts and improve UI event fidelity. This is intentionally messy — capturing hypotheses, quick probes, and what to bake into the canary run next week.

Attendees:
- Aisha Raman (owner)
- Marco Villanueva (frontend)
- Jin Park (observability)
- Priya Desai (analytics)
- Noah Greene (QA) — dial-in later for smoke

Agenda:
1) Revisit last sprint spike on event dedup heuristics (RDI-3421)
2) Quick experiment: client-side batching vs. server-side dedup for panel-open events
3) Define metric baseline and success criteria for canary
4) Decide instrumentation gaps + short tasks for next 48h

Notes / Observations:
- Problem: ~18% of panel-open events are duplicates (same session, <2s apart). Downstream aggregation blows up counts in per-route dashboards and skews anomaly detectors.
- Current heuristic: frontend drops events with identical panelId within 1s. Too aggressive (we lose fast user interactions), and inconsistent across mobile/web.
- Analytics wants canonical events with session_id + interaction_index to simplify joins; that requires adding a tiny counter to panel component (cheap) but will require SDK bump.

Hypotheses:
H1: Client-side lightweight de-dup (session_id + short ttl) reduces duplicate rate by >50% without losing real interactions.
H2: Server-side dedup using KV cache (TTL 3s) can reduce duplicates more but adds cost and complexity for Dedicated / Private where routing differs.
H3: Instrumenting a per-panel interaction_index will make downstream joins 10x more straightforward and allow us to remove brittle time-window heuristics.

Experiment plan (quick probes run in lab):
- Probe A (client-batching): Add transient interaction_index in localStorage (unique per session), UI increments on every panel-open. SDK emits event with {session_id, interaction_index}. We run against canary frontends for 48h.
- Probe B (server-dedupe): Route events to a staging dedupe endpoint that keeps a 3s in-memory LRU of (session_id, panel_id, interaction_index absent). If duplicate within ttl, drop.
- Probe C (no-change control): current heuristic, but with richer logging to understand false positives/negatives.

Lab measurements (first 24h):
- Baseline duplicate rate (control): 18.2% duplicates (sample: 120k panel-open events)
- Probe A (client-batching): duplicates 7.9% (sample: 46k) — big win but we saw 0.6% of events that look like real double-opens (user genuinely opened+closed+reopened) flagged as duplicate because of session edge-case (session recreate).
- Probe B (server-dedupe): duplicates 4.1% (sample: 62k) — best reduction but introduced a spike in latency for the event ingestion path (~45ms p95 added) under heavy concurrent bursts.
- False positives: both approaches reduced duplicates but client approach had slightly more FP on mobile due to session_id churn on backgrounding.

Quick SQL snippets used (ad-hoc):
- Identify repeated opens:
  SELECT session_id, panel_id, COUNT(*) as c, MIN(ts) as first_ts, MAX(ts) as last_ts
  FROM panel_events_sample
  WHERE event_type='panel_open' AND ts > now() - interval '2 days'
  GROUP BY session_id, panel_id
  HAVING MIN(ts) != MAX(ts)
  ORDER BY c DESC

Decisions from sync:
- Short-term: ship Probe A (client increment) to a canary cohort (10% web, 0% mobile) next Wed AM. Rationale: low-risk, no server impact, quick SDK bump.
- Mid-term: pursue server-dedupe as opt-in path for Dedicated customers who prefer server-side smoothing; requires infra perf review.
- Instrumentation: add interaction_index to panel-events payload (required by both probes). Ticket created (RDI-3514).

Open gaps / Risks:
- Mobile session churn causes interaction_index collisions — need session stabilization work (Priya to pair with mobile eng).
- Server dedupe memory/rate cost unknown at scale; Jin volunteered to run a perf run against a 1M events/min supermarket trace.
- Alerts: current anomaly detector should not be retrained until we stabilize the canonical event shape — otherwise we will get lots of false positives during rollout.

Action items (owner — due):
- Aisha: draft canary rollout doc + gating checklist (due 2027-02-15) — include SDK bump notes and rollback plan.
- Marco: PR for client interaction_index + feature flag; target code freeze EOD 2027-02-13. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1287 (WIP).
- Priya: carve out mobile-session-churn spike analysis; pair with mobile eng (due 2027-02-14).
- Jin: perf-run server-dedupe on staging dataset; post numbers to the dashboard (due 2027-02-16).
- Noah: smoke test plan for canary (makelist of acceptance checks + quick harness) (due 2027-02-15).

Monitoring & Success criteria for canary:
- Metric: duplicate_rate(panel_open) drop from baseline 18.2% -> <=9% in canary cohort within 24h.
- No meaningful increase in event ingestion p95 (>10ms) for the overall pipeline in canary.
- No spike in downstream alert noise (false-positive rate on route-anomaly detector) for 48h post-rollout.

Notes to follow up in next sync:
- If client canary meets target, schedule 50% web canary and a small mobile pilot with session fixes.
- If server dedupe perf numbers are promising, sketch an infra cost model for Dedicated customers.

Random lab artifacts / snippets:
- Local test harness: scripts/telemetry/dedupe_sim.py (toy sim used to estimate memory footprint)
- Quick dashboard: console/panel-telemetry-v2 -> view: dedupe-experiment-2027-02-11

Misc / Brain dump:
- Consider a hybrid: client adds interaction_index; servers keep a very short TTL cache to catch cases where client session resets mid-interaction. That might yield the lowest FP with tolerable cost.
- We should also add a small TTL to the interaction_index server-side (e.g., 10s) so we can safely re-emit events during network blips without training detectors on duplicates.

Meeting adjourned — leaving notes here as canonical lab log. Will convert to a polished canary doc once Probe A PR merges and Jin posts perf numbers.

-- Aisha
